title: Execution of the capacity-check routine
statement: Fix a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over Boolean symbols and a computation mode. Let $y$ be an input word, $B$ a register bound, $w$ a Boolean word, and $v$ an initial assignment of natural numbers to the $21$ registers. Suppose every register value is at most $B$, the length register equals the position register plus the length of $w$, and, at each position $i<|w|$, the input bit at the position register plus $i$ equals the $i$th bit of $w$ (with false used for out-of-range reads). Then there is an assignment $v'$ such that every register remains at most $B$, the position register does not increase, and every register other than the position and capacity registers is unchanged. The specified register program has a guarded execution from the capacity-check routine and $v$ to the state determined by whether $|w|$ is at most the binary length of the capacity register's initial value and whether the last bit of $w$ (defaulting to true when $w$ is empty) is true: it continues to the designated next routine exactly when both conditions hold, and otherwise rejects.
